text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- State-owned SNCF railway operator chairman Louis Gallois calls for restructuring and decentralisation, wants to move headquarters out of Paris, aims for breakeven in 1998.
-- Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean Peyrelevade to present first-half results on Thursday, may announce new bailout plan.
-- Labour Minister Jaques Barrot expected to present measures today to curb social security deficit to 30 billion francs from an estimated 47 billion for 1997.
LA TRIBUNE DESFOSSES
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis calls in an interview for a European political stability council to support monetary stability and balance the power of a future European central bank.
-- Car sales expected to soar in September ahead of the expiry at the end of the month of a government incentive scheme.
-- Some members of parliament call for renewed ceiling on income tax for wealthiest taxpayers.
-- IBM to reshuffle its computer services activities in France, merge Axone and CGI.
L'AGEFI
-- State may consider selling minority stakes in Pechiney Usinor, CLF, Seita, Roussel-Uclaf.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Swiss temporary-work group Adecco formed by the merger of Ecco and Adia aims to conquer 10 percent of the global temporary workers' market.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- BNP, Societe Generale and savings bank Caisses d'Epargne may be interested in buying state-owned CIC bank.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- EU's single currency drive gets a boost in Dublin.
-- Olivetti in talks with France Telecom that could lead to France Telecom buying an equity stake in the Italian group.
